subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should browser private-network SSRF handling gain core confirmation, allow/block, or temporary-grant semantics, and which first-stage policy shape should become the supported contract?
rationale: The request changes browser egress security semantics and public config/CLI surface; current source has no approval or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve staged policy first
options.body: Define explicit allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata/link-local behavior, docs, and tests before considering interactive prompts.

options.title: Approve interactive confirmation now
options.body: Commit to user approval UX with timeout, rate limiting, session scoping, and audit behavior across browser navigation paths.

options.title: Keep current strict model
options.body: Continue with strict default plus host exceptions and document broad private-network access as a trusted-environment opt-in only.

recommendation.title: Approve staged policy first
recommendation.body: Define explicit allow/block semantics, non-overridable metadata/link-local behavior, docs, and tests before considering interactive prompts.

likelyOwner.reason: This account has the strongest recent history across SSRF helpers, browser config/docs, and adjacent browser security fixes.
